item.title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. Across tested model-harness combinations, out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation. Errors typically originate from cross-stage inconsistencies that surface only several stages after they are introduced. We therefore develop AI-Donkey, an agentic framework that combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to enable high-fidelity GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations and analyses. With AI-Donkey, all tested agents, from frontier proprietary models to open-weight models, produce complete, runnable MBPT workflows with no observed run-to-run variation. We further demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials, including the many-body enhancement of Fr\"ohlich electron-phonon coupling in polar semiconductors. Our approach provides a general framework for knowledge engineering to enable reliable agentic workflows in computational materials science.
item.dc:creator: Benran Zhang, Byeongchan Lee, Zien Zhu, Chih-En Hsu, Zhenfa Zheng, Hung-Chung Hsueh, Young Woo Choi, Mauro Del Ben, Zhenglu Li

item.title: Identifying intercalation electrodes for electrochemical ion recovery and desalination
item.description: arXiv:2610.20834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). Among myriad ion capture techniques, we focus on electrochemical methods using intercalation electrodes, an energy-efficient approach capable of both selectively extracting specific ions or non-selectively extracting multiple ions from diverse water sources. However, practical realization of electrochemical ion capture requires the use of robust cation intercalation electrodes, with the state-of-the-art olivine-FePO$_4$ and spinel-Mn$_2$O$_4$ exhibiting several shortcomings. Thus, we develop a high-throughput computational workflow to identify potential intercalation electrodes for both ion recovery and desalination from a pool of 20,414 Li, Mg, Ca, Na, and/or K-containing structures from the Materials Project database. Based on the construction of Pourbaix diagrams relevant for electrodes operating under seawater conditions, modifying criteria used for defining metastability in seawater, computing average intercalation voltages and the extent of metastability of electrode structures, and computational graphs to encode ionic selectivity, we identify a total of 11 promising electrodes for selective ion recovery and one possible desalination electrode. The promising materials identified in this work include Fe$_2$(MoO$_4$)$_3$, Li$_3$Fe$_2$(PO$_4$)$_3$, LiFeP$_2$O$_7$ for selective Li-recovery. Our study provides thermodynamic insights, qualitative trends, and a promising list of intercalation electrodes for experimental testing that should advance the field of electrochemical ion recovery.
item.dc:creator: Sougat Purohit, Andreas Kuhlmann, Marten Huck, Hans-Georg Steinr\"uck, Gopalakrishnan Sai Gautam

item.title: Transition-Metal-Oxygen Covalency Controls Ligand-Hole Stability in Li-Rich Cathode
item.description: arXiv:2610.20837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium-rich cathodes boast a large specific capacity due to the presence of excess lithium per transition metal. However, making use of that excess Li drives the cathodes to unusually high formal oxidation states, often triggering unwanted side reactions, typically signaled by gas release and commonly associated with oxygen oxidation. By varying the transition metal (TM) chemistry in Li-rich materials, cyclability can vary drastically, with some materials suffering rapid capacity fade while others are able to maintain large and stable voltage windows. Such observations indicate a crucial role for both TM and O activities, but the details remain elusive. Here, we model core-level spectroscopy to understand differences in the charge compensation mechanism between different Li2MO3 (M = Mn, Ru, Ir) cathode materials. We find that ligand holes are important throughout the series, but their stability depends strongly on the transition-metal-oxygen electronic structure. In Li2MnO3, the ground state is already strongly negative-charge-transfer-like, so further delithiation rapidly increases ligand-hole character and promotes instability. Moving from Mn to Ru and Ir increases TM-O hybridization while reducing the tendency toward an extreme negative-charge-transfer state, allowing additional holes to remain delocalized over the covalent TM-O network over a wider range of charge. These results identify TM-O covalency, rather than the absence of oxygen-hole character, as a key factor controlling reversible high-valent redox and suggest a route for stabilizing high-energy-density cathodes without invoking reversible molecular oxygen formation.
item.dc:creator: Kuan H. Hsu, Eder G. Lomeli, Jaehoon Kim, Gukhyun Lim, Amelia Zhao, Wen-Shin Lu, Joshua J. Kas, John Vinson, Brian Moritz, Jihyun Hong, Wanli Yang, Thomas P. Devereaux

item.title: Grain-Size Dependence of Thermal and Electrical Properties in (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-{\delta} High-Entropy Carbide Ceramics
item.description: arXiv:2610.20864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal and electrical transport in high-entropy carbides can be influenced by grain-boundary scattering, but the relevant microstructural regime remains uncertain. Here, near-fully dense $(Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C_{1-{\delta}}$ ceramics were densified by spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 {\deg}C, producing average grain sizes from 9.3 $\pm$ 4.9 to 28.8 $\pm$ 15.3 $\mu$m while retaining the rock-salt phase. Heat capacities were measured experimentally and estimated by the Neumann-Kopp law with the latter used to calculate thermal conductivity. Thermal conductivity values were in the range of 6.8-7.1 W $m^{-1}$ $K^{-1}$ at room temperature, but showed no systematic dependence on grain size within the investigated range. Room-temperature electrical resistivity values were in the range of 151.9 to 177.0 $\mu{\Omega}$ cm and likewise showed no grain-size dependence. The electron contribution to room-temperature thermal conductivity was estimated to be approximately 58-68% of total thermal conductivity as estimated using the Wiedemann-Franz law and the theoretical Lorenz number. The results indicated that processing-induced grain coarsening did not produce clearly resolvable transport-property changes under the conditions investigated leading to the conclusion that intrinsic disorder and defect chemistry may exert stronger influences on properties.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sarikhani, Gregory E. Hilmas, David W. Lipke, Douglas E. Wolfe, Stefano Curtarolo, Shen J. Dillon, William G. Fahrenholtz

item.title: Sb-5$p$-mediated antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in the intermetallic 4$f$-3$d$-5$p$ compound Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$ by means of high-field x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) spectroscopy, complemented by magnetization measurements and density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. This coupling is unexpected for intermetallics composed of light rare-earth and transition-metal elements. Sb $M_{4,5}$-edge XMCD measurements indicate a clear spin polarization of Sb 5$p$ states antiparallel to the Fe 3$d$ moments. DFT calculations reveal the site-dependent character of the Sb moments and, together with the Fe-Sb antiparallel alignment seen by XMCD, identify a Fe 3$d$-Sb 5$p$-Nd 5$d$ hybridization pathway for the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling. Pulsed-field XMCD reveals a field-induced spin reorientation through the evolution of the $c$-axis projections of the Nd and Fe moments. Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$, thus, provides a platform for exploring antiparallel rare-earth-transition-metal ($R$-$T$) coupling mediated by transition-metal 3$d$-ligand $p$-rare-earth 5$d$ hybridization in light-$R$-$T$ intermetallics with $p$-elements.
item.dc:creator: S. Palazzese, Sh. Yamamoto, T. Kotte, R. Ray, F. Pabst, S. Chattopadhyay, D. I. Gorbunov, T. Herrmannsd\"orfer, K. Kummer, A. Kurtanidze, E. Weschke, O. Prokhnenko, K. Yamamoto, Y. Kotani, H. Nojiri, M. Ruck, Manuel Richter, J. Wosnitza

item.title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
item.description: arXiv:2610.20886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct injection of charge from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed molecules via the chemical interface damping of localized surface plasmons has emerged as a promising avenue to avoid the rapid thermalization of hot carriers. In this paper, we develop an approach for predicting hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles into adsorbed carbon monoxide (CO) molecules. The approach combines a detailed description of the adsorbate-metal interactions via ab initio density functional theory with a macroscopic electrodynamics treatment of the localized surface plasmon. We apply this approach to nine different metals including both traditional (Ag, Au, Cu) and emerging (Al) plasmonic metals as well as non-plasmonic metals (Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt). For all metals, hot-electron injection is larger than hot-hole injection. This is a consequence of the alignment of the CO frontier orbitals, with the CO lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) being closer to the metal Fermi energy than the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO). The largest electron injection rates in the optical photon ranges are obtained for Al, Ag, Cu and Au, with Cu and Au showing significant plasmonic enhancement. The non-plasmonic metals show weak electron injection as a consequence of their high LUMO energies relative to the metal Fermi level. The results of our study pave the way towards a rational design of metallic nanoscale photocatalysts for specific chemical processes.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Alan Edwards, Johannes Lischner

item.title: MASON: Materials Atomistic Structure builder Operated in Natural language
item.description: arXiv:2610.21015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building reliable atomistic models is a critical and often challenging step in first-principles calculations. Although large language model agents can assist with structure generation, they lack direct capabilities for crystallographic operations and therefore struggle to construct complex structures reliably. Here we present MASON, an AI-native toolkit for atomistic structure construction that can be invoked by agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In an end-to-end example, an agent builds a CO/Pt(111) adsorption model from a natural language request. By equipping agents with dedicated structure-building tools, MASON enables reliable and efficient atomistic model construction and provides a foundation for autonomous first-principles workflows.
item.dc:creator: Xinyue Zhang, Jixiang Li, Bin Shao, Baishun Yang, Zhiyang Liu, Weichao Wang

item.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena
item.description: arXiv:2610.21050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Soft porous crystals can undergo guest-induced structural transitions producing unconventional adsorption isotherms, which are valuable for gas separation and storage applications. However, the evidence for these transitions is scattered across the literature in narrative form and has not been aggregated. Here we use a large language model pipeline to mine the literature for anomalous adsorption, extracting phase-transition events together with material, adsorbate, temperature and pressure metadata and classifying each into an established behavioural class. Benchmarked against human annotation, the extraction stage attains an F1 score of 0.96. When applied at scale, the pipeline yields a curated corpus of 547 transitions across 240 distinct materials, drawn from 200 of 4,252 screened publications, which we further link to crystallographic structures. Analysis of this database shows that the principal behavioural classes, gate-opening and breathing, are distinguished by their functional response. Gate-opening frameworks transform at a significantly lower pressure than breathing frameworks (p = 3.8E-3). In contrast, no difference in pore size, void fraction, linker chemistry or metal identity was detected between the classes. Our findings argue for a functional rather than purely structural description of responsive porous materials. They also highlight the need for a community database that records the guest, temperature and pressure of every reported transition of these materials.
item.dc:creator: Fengxu Yang, Matthew L. Schneider, Weitong Chen, Jack D. Evans

item.title: Broadband radio-frequency TEM specimen holders for in situ biasing excitation and 100-ps-scale electron beam control
item.description: arXiv:2610.21275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband electrical excitation inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) is required to investigate electrically driven nanodevices at their actual operating frequencies and to develop fully electrical time-resolved experiments at a sub-nanosecond range. Here, we report the performances of homemade two- and four-channel radio-frequency (RF) TEM specimen holders based on a hybrid architecture combining coaxial transmission lines with miniaturized impedance-controlled printed circuit boards (PCB). Removable mechanical contacts provide direct electrical connection to interchangeable TEM chips without wire bonding. Vector network analyzer measurements demonstrate broadband transmission through the complete electrical path up to the specimen. With a representative TEM chip, the two-channel holder exhibits a -3 dB bandwidth of 7.9 GHz, while insertion losses remain below 12 dB up to 18 GHz. The same RF holder architecture was used to drive a miniaturized electrostatic electron-beam deflector. The measured temporal response indicates that the holder deflector assembly remains compatible with electrical pulse durations approaching 100 ps, with the shortest accessible times presently limited by the available waveform generator. High-resolution TEM imaging with a 200 ps probe window does not show detectable degradation of spatial resolution, while off-axis electron holography is successfully performed for probe durations down to 0.5 ns under conditions representative of operando measurements. These results establish a versatile broadband platform combining GHz electrical excitation and sub-nanosecond electron-beam control. The dual-stage configuration of our Hitachi HF3300 microscope further provides the basis for a future fully electrical pump-probe TEM approach using independently driven RF holders for specimen excitation and electron-probe control.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Gatel, Marine Resano, B\'erang\`ere Disic, Nasibeh Parsaei, Emmanuel Perrin, Herv\'e Parvery, Romain Queslier, Bertrand Gatti, Pierre Abeilhou, Alexandre Alibert, Christian Pertel, C\'ecile Marcelot, Nicolas Biziere

item.title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
item.description: arXiv:2610.21563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi

item.title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
item.description: arXiv:2610.21618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial visual synapses combine sensing, memory and processing in a single device, but most of them need an external voltage to read the synaptic weight and light is generally able to strengthen the weight rather than to weaken it. We report here Se/ZnMgO thin film photodiodes in which the photocurrent at zero bias writes and reads the synaptic weight, with a direction of change set by the photon energy alone. At equal photon flux, 365 nm pulses increase the photocurrent by 38 % while 455 nm pulses decrease it, and the depression reaching 30 % at higher flux, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch and no electrical energy spent. Spectrally resolved light soaking shows that short wavelengths potentiate while low-energy light erases. The interesting property is therefore the photon energy-dependent competition between potentiation and depression, the crossover being set by the defect population of the interface. Optical simulations show that both wavelengths are absorbed within the first tens of nanometres of Se, and the stored state is erased by a reverse bias in a voltage-dependent way and by sub-gap light, which indicates that potentiation corresponds to interface defects filled with electrons, in agreement with drift-diffusion simulations. The devices also show relearning, their response is modulated by bending on flexible substrates, and a network built from the measured weight updates reaches 89 % accuracy on handwritten digit recognition without noise and 85 % with the measured noise, against 97.5 % for floating-point weights.
item.dc:creator: Zacharie Jehl Li-Kao, Miho Akasaka, Myeongok Kim, Kunal J. Tiwari, Antoine Moore, Mykhailo A. Koltsov, Sergio Giraldo, Saiki Kitagawa, Marcel Placidi, Taizo Kobayashi

item.title: Directed impulsive molecular dynamics reveal energy-routing pathways of bond cleavage in TATB
item.description: arXiv:2610.21637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Responses of energetic materials to external stimuli involve more than uniform thermalization. Understanding directional energy redistribution is essential for structural and ignition design. Here, we use TATB as an example to construct a vibrationally faithful machine-learning potential from only 4,630 configurations. To resolve the elusive nonequilibrium energy flow, we develop directed impulsive molecular dynamics, a statistically controlled protocol that repeatedly deposits equal kinetic energy along selected vibrational modes. By amplifying mode-specific responses while tracking the ensuing nonequilibrium evolution, this approach turns energy redistribution into a directly traceable routing process. We find that initial bond cleavage depends strongly on the initially excited mode, rather than being determined by bond-cleavage barriers alone. Specifically, modes that readily trigger reaction efficiently channel energy towards a bond cleavage coordinate, whereas modes that are less effective at inducing break divert energy into soft-like modes or trap it in modes from which energy flow is inefficient.
item.dc:creator: Guanchen Dong, Xiaona Huang, Yuxuan Chen, Linghua Tan, Guangcheng Yang, Rui Su, Lin Wang, Pengfei Guan

item.title: Defect Candidates for Single-Photon Emission in Monolayer GaS and GaSe
item.description: arXiv:2610.21670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spin-resolved electronic structure of native vacancies and substitutional defects in monolayer GaS and GaSe using an anisotropic screened-exchange functional developed for two-dimensional material systems. By combining an energy-based classification of defect-associated states with spatially resolved projections and partial charge densities, we examine how these defects modify the in-gap electronic structure and assess their relevance for defect-based single-photon emission. The results identify gallium vacancies, particularly in GaS, as candidates single-photon emitters.
item.dc:creator: Michael Lorke

item.title: Novel high-pressure silicon allotrope with quartz topology from first principles
item.description: arXiv:2610.21683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel silicon allotrope, qtz Si, with quartz topology is proposed and investigated alongside four known allotropes (dia Si-I, lon Si-IV, bsn Si-II, and gsi Si-III) using first-principles density functional theory. qtz Si is found to exhibit the smallest atom-averaged volume (18.06 A3), highest density (2.582 g/cm3), highest bulk modulus (98 GPa), and highest maximum phonon frequency (16 THz) among the five, while showing the lowest shear modulus (37 GPa). All five allotropes are confirmed to satisfy the Born stability criteria and to display positive phonon frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, i.e., they are mechanically and dynamically stable. Electronic structure calculations show that qtz Si is a semimetal with a vanishing gap, whereas dia Si and lon Si are semiconductors, and bsn and gsi allotropes are weakly metallic. Energy-volume equations of state place gsi and qtz 0.11-0.15 eV/atom above dia, bsn, and lon, consistent with their identification as high-pressure or metastable phases.
item.dc:creator: Samir F. Matar, Vladimir L. Solozhenko

item.title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
item.description: arXiv:2610.21718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) control their local structure and influence a broad range of mechanical and thermodynamic properties. Yet they are notoriously difficult to identify. Locating low-energy ordered candidates requires exploring a configurational space that grows combinatorially with the number of elements, and Monte Carlo searches driven by density-functional theory (DFT) need a new electronic-structure calculation at every trial step. Here we introduce MECx (Minimum Energy Configuration eXplorer), a framework that guides Monte Carlo searches with a surrogate energy model trained on configurations stratified in bond-count space. Applied to ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys using compact training sets of 100 DFT-labeled configurations, MECx identifies ordered configurations with lower energies than those found by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits. These configurations exhibit distinct pair-specific ordering, including B2- and B32-like motifs, and undergo progressive disordering as temperature increases. The MPEA-trained models also transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining. The resulting ordered configurations agree with those obtained by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and produce experimentally distinguishable superlattice reflections in simulated neutron diffraction patterns.
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Arora, Alex Tai, Rodrigo Freitas, David Cereceda

item.title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,\mu_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. EuSe combines a saturation magnetization of 1100 kA/m with antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic phases that are reached with fields below 0.25 T. In contrast to a Gilbert-damped ferromagnet, the linewidth of the field-aligned film decreases with increasing frequency and field, and below 750 mK it no longer depends on temperature. At 30 mK, 68 GHz and 1.8 T, it reaches 5.5 mT, close to the values of bulk single crystals, which corresponds to a magnon lifetime of 2 ns and to an upper bound of $1.1\times10^{-3}$ for the Gilbert damping parameter. These properties make EuSe and the europium chalcogenides promising materials for hybrid quantum systems and quantum magnonics.
item.dc:creator: Rostyslav O. Serha, Jan Hofer, Khrystyna O. Levchenko, Andreas Ney, Sergej O. Demokritov, Gunther Springholz, Andrii V. Chumak

item.title: Coexistence of Altermagnetic and Compensated Ferrimagnetic Motifs in a Noncollinear Multiferroic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collinear compensated magnets with nonrelativistic spin splitting comprise altermagnets (ALMs), whose rotation- or mirror-related opposite-spin sublattices produce momentum-selective splitting that vanishes at $\Gamma$, and compensated ferrimagnets (CFIMs), whose symmetry-inequivalent sublattices allow splitting throughout the Brillouin zone, including at $\Gamma$. Here, we show that the coplanar noncollinear magnetic state of multiferroic boracite Ni$_3$B$_7$O$_{13}$Cl hosts both motifs on distinct Ni sublattices in real space. The electronic structure and spin texture exhibit coexisting $d$-wave-like and $s$-wave-like spin-polarization components associated with the ALM and CFIM motifs, respectively. Opposite ferroelectric states exhibit reversed band-resolved spin polarizations, indicating magnetoelectric coupling, and sign reversals of linear shift and circular injection currents.
item.dc:creator: Vikrant Chaudhary, Fu Li, Hui Liu, Mengli Hu, Rajyavardhan Ray, Chen Shen, Jeroen van den Brink, Hongbin Zhang, Harish K. Singh

item.title: Large in-plane optical anisotropy in epitaxial CrN(113) films
item.description: arXiv:2610.21856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CrN, a transition-metal nitride crystallizing in the cubic rocksalt structure, exhibits a unique combination of mechanical robustness, semiconducting behavior, and thermoelectric functionality. To date, however, CrN has been synthesized primarily as polycrystalline material or as epitaxial films grown along high-symmetry orientations such as (001) and (111). Here, we prepare epitaxial CrN(113) films on AlN(11\bar{2}2) templates by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. The low-symmetry interface and highly direction dependent lattice mismatch are expected to modify the physical properties of CrN relative to the bulk material. Indeed, variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry in the photon-energy range from 1.25 to 5 eV reveals a surprisingly strong polarization dependence of the optical response despite the nearly strain-free cubic crystal structure of the films. The pseudo-optical constants n and k differ by more than 10% for orthogonal in-plane polarizations throughout the investigated spectral range. We evaluate possible origins of this effect and conclude that it most likely arises from anisotropic surface morphology of CrN(113), which creates a metasurface acting as a subwavelength grating in the strongly absorbing regime.
item.dc:creator: Duc V. Dinh, Frank Peiris, Oliver Brandt

item.title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel A. Lazar, Chris H. Rycroft

item.title: Coherent and Incoherent Time-Resolved Diffuse Scattering Intensity from First Principles
item.description: arXiv:2610.22006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved diffuse scattering from X-ray free-electron lasers and ultrafast electron diffraction gives access to the nonequilibrium lattice dynamics of photoexcited solids in reciprocal space. Existing interpretations have often relied on simplified models. Here we present a first-principles formulation of the time-dependent first-order diffuse intensity in which coherent and incoherent contributions emerge on equal footing. By assuming the probe-pulse coherence time to be longer than the characteristic electronic timescales, but shorter than those of the ionic motion, we work in the density-matrix formalism and derive equations of motion for the displacement-displacement correlators in a basis of instantaneous, out-of-equilibrium Born-Oppenheimer normal modes. We show how the incoherent contribution, governed by the phonon occupations, and a coherent contribution, governed by the anomalous phonon correlators, emerge. The non-trivial coherent dynamics is shown to be induced both by the photoinduced phonon-frequency shift and by electron-phonon scattering off the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. We implement the resulting equations using Wannier interpolation in the \textsc{EPI}q code and apply them to photoexcited germanium. The calculated diffuse intensity reproduces both the oscillation frequencies and the rising incoherent background observed experimentally, opening the way to a systematic interpretation of time-resolved diffuse scattering in ultrafast experiments.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Furci, Giovanni Marini, Stefano Mocatti, Matteo Calandra

item.title: From picometre displacements to a three-dimensional lattice gas of polar skyrmions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polar skyrmions, the electric analogues of magnetic skyrmions, form arrays in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices that are known to be only short-range ordered, but how this disordered ensemble is organized in three dimensions, and how its microscopic structure underlies this organization, have remained largely inaccessible. Here, using three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-{\Delta}PDF) analysis of X-ray diffuse scattering, we show that the polar skyrmion bubbles form a three-dimensional lattice gas: they occupy discrete sites, but their order extends over only a few neighbours and is two to three times stronger across the SrTiO3 spacers than within a layer. This interlayer coupling is consistent with the polarization of the bubbles extending into the spacers. Within each bubble, the polarization rotates in a predominantly N\'eel-type manner, and Pb and Ti rotate together with comparable picometre displacements, demonstrating that both A- and B-site cations take part in the polar distortion.
item.dc:creator: Joohee Bang, Nives Strkalj, Hugo Aramberri, Stephan Rosenkranz, Arkadiy Simonov, Morgan Trassin, Thomas Weber

item.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Machine Learning for Fracture Prediction in Heterogeneous Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.20614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding fracture behavior is critical for assessing the structural integrity and longevity. Highly time-consuming physics-based fracture simulations motivate the development of machine-learning-based fracture evolution prediction with surrogate models. However, most existing machine-learning models for fracture prediction operate as black boxes and require large training datasets to generalize reliably. In this work, Thermodynamically Consistent Latent Dynamics Identification (tLaSDI) for parametric systems is introduced to predict fracture patterns and evolution in heterogeneous materials. The model learns the thermodynamic state variable in a lower-dimensional latent space using parametric GENERIC Formalism-Informed Neural Networks (pGFINNs) that enforce key thermodynamic principles, such as total energy conservation and entropy generation. This model embeds physics into the neural network architecture using a hard-constraint method that inherently complies with the underlying thermodynamic principles. The proposed tLaSDI-pGFINNs is further enhanced by a Geometry-Conditioned Autoencoder in learning the geometry configuration for effective geometry-guided learning. The energy and entropy evolution histories demonstrate that the model preserves the thermodynamic constraints on unseen testing samples. The results further show that tLaSDI-pGFINNs can more accurately capture both fracture patterns and the subsequent fracture evolution than the purely data-driven Autoencoder Long Short-Term Memory (AE-LSTM) model.
item.dc:creator: Muhamad Alim, Xiaolong He, Mei-Na Tsao, Chi-Hua Yu, J. S. Chen

item.title: Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.20624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Damage prediction in particulate elastomeric composites is challenging due to the strong material heterogeneity, nearly incompressible behavior of the matrix, and the presence of localized stress concentrations arising from matrix-inclusion interactions. In the present work, a computational framework is developed for damage propagation analysis of particulate elastomeric composite structures. The effective constitutive response of the heterogeneous material is first determined using the second-order homogenization method. The resulting homogenized response is subsequently used to identify equivalent hyperelastic material parameters for structural simulations. A three-parameter isotropic damage model is incorporated to capture damage-induced softening. A mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation, is used to alleviate volumetric locking associated with nearly incompressible property of elastomers. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale simulations and homogenized response involving composites with varying inclusion volume fractions. Numerical investigations demonstrate that the homogenized models is able to reproduce the global force-displacement response within 2% error and damage evolution characteristics of the heterogeneous composites while significantly reducing the computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Murthy Pabbu, Tarkes Dora Pallicity, Nelson Muthu

item.title: Crystallization of the undertile
item.description: arXiv:2610.20663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify all periodic tilings with a monotile known as $\mathbf{R1}$ and called here the undertile, which underlies several aperiodic monotiles such as the Taylor-Socolar one. The classification is done using deflation, through a study of fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed. A full classification of fracture patterns is given, that also applies to non-periodic tilings with the undertile. This can be used to reprove non-periodicity of some existing monotiles based on the undertile.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Ch\'eritat

item.title: Resonant enhancement of Raman scattering in a MoS$_2$ nanotube
item.description: arXiv:2610.20755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The whispering-gallery modes confined in the wall of a multiwall MoS$_2$ nanotube resonantly enhance the spontaneous Raman scattering by its own optical phonons. The enhancement is doubly resonant --- pump and Stokes waves hit two adjacent modes at one pump energy, and the signal scales as $(Q_{\rm pump}Q_{\rm sc})^2$ - whenever a phonon energy matches the free spectral range of the mode ladder. Near the A exciton the excitonic dispersion compresses the ladder and sweeps its spacing through all intralayer phonon energies of MoS$_2$, so the match, reached for $A_{1g}$ at $E_{\rm pump}=1551$~meV, requires no geometric tuning. A missed match splits the excitation peak into a pump- and a scattered-resonant doublet whose splitting measures the residual detuning. Selection rules confine the double resonance to the TM$\to$TM channel and exclude $E_{1g}$.
item.dc:creator: D. R. Kazanov, A. V. Poshakinskiy

item.title: Universal Dynamic Scaling for Sub-Yield Aging and Over-Yield Rejuvenation in A Cyclically Driven Metallic Glass
item.description: arXiv:2610.21625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether sub-yield aging and over-yield rejuvenation in cyclically deformed amorphous solids share a common physical origin or arise from distinct microscopic mechanisms remains a fundamental yet unresolved debate. Using molecular dynamics simulations of a metallic glass, we resolve this duality by uncovering a unified dynamic clock that dictates energy landscape navigation across both regimes. We show that the transition between regimes reflects a fundamental shift in energy injection pathways: (i) In the over-yield regime, rejuvenation is driven as a first-order response to macroscopic plastic shear work derived from Herschel-Bulkley non-linear rheological scaling. (ii) In contrast, this macroscopic work scaling fails in the sub-yield regime, where early-stage energy landscape elevation and subsequent cyclic aging are instead governed by second-order localized elastic stress fluctuations acting as a mechanical catalyst and noise source, respectively. Intense high-rate agitation increases the escape probability from deeper potential energy minima, thereby suppressing the retention efficiency of structural relaxation. By identifying these localized fluctuations as the primary origin of rate-attenuated sub-yield relaxation, we establish an exact scaling identity relating the relaxation attenuation exponent to the stress fluctuation exponent. This work directly bridges non-linear rheology with stress fluctuation dynamics, providing a unified framework to predict and manipulate structural evolution in amorphous solids.
item.dc:creator: Nannan Ren, Hongfei Zhang, Rui Wan, Pengfei Guan, Limin Wang, Baoshuang Shang

item.title: Interlocked Vortex Order in the Frustrated $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ Lattice ($A$=Cs,Rb)
item.description: arXiv:2610.21854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently synthesized $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ ($A$ = Cs, Rb) provides a unique platform for exploring the interplay between geometric frustration, magnetism, and correlated electronic states beyond conventional kagome systems. Based on first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the frustrated V sublattice naturally stabilizes a robust vortex or anti-vortex antiferromagnetic ground state, whose total energy is substantially lower than all other configurations. In addition, the Heisenberg model analysis show strong constraints on the ground state magnetic configuration, such that fixing spin configuration of 1 triangle propagates and fixes all others. The vortex or anti-vortex phase hosts electronic structures reminiscent of kagome metals, including Dirac-like band crossings, van Hove singularities, and flat bands near the Fermi level. Owing to the noncollinear spin texture and quasi-two-dimensional magnetic character, the N\'eel temperature exhibits an extremely weak dependence on both the magnitude and direction of external magnetic fields, consistent with experimental observations. For Cs-based compound, the ground state band structure is metallic with 6 Weyl points in the BZ; while for the Rb-based compound, spin--orbit coupling opens an approximately 27-meV gap at ambient pressure due to the lifted C$_3$ symmetry. Our results establish $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ as a promising platform for studying frustration-driven chiral magnetism and its interplay with topological electronic states.
item.dc:creator: Zilong Li, H. -Q. Yuan, Xiaoqun Wang, Chao Cao

item.title: Pt-induced semimetallic transport and enhanced thermoelectric response in the half-Heusler alloy YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi
item.description: arXiv:2610.22253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Half-Heusler alloys provide a versatile platform for tuning electronic and thermal transport through chemical substitution. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric and magnetotransport properties of spark-plasma-sintered YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi. Partial substitution of Ni by Pt drives YNiBi toward semimetallic transport, characterized by hole-dominated conduction, a low Hall carrier concentration of $\mathrm{1.9 \times 10^{19} cm^{-3}}$, and a sizeable nonsaturating magnetoresistance of 18$\%$ at 300 K under 14 T. Compared with YNiBi, Pt alloying increases the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient from approximately 90 to 130 $\mathrm{\mu V K^{-1}}$, while reducing the thermal conductivity to 3.15 $\mathrm{W m^{-1} K^{-1}}$. Single-parabolic-band analysis indicates an enhanced carrier effective mass, resulting in a room-temperature power factor of 13.7 $\mathrm{\mu W cm^{-1} K^{-2}}$ and a figure of merit ($zT$= 0.13). First-principles calculations further show a Pt-induced closing of the electronic band gap and a low density of states near the Fermi level, consistent with the experimentally observed semimetal-like transport. These results demonstrate that Ni/Pt alloying provides an effective route for simultaneously tuning the electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties of YNiBi-based half-Heusler compounds.
item.dc:creator: Vikas Chahar, Shivam Rathod, Lankun Wang, Sneh, Shubhadeep Bej, Divya Prakash Dubey, Dinesh Dixit, Abdelmoneim Elkhouly, Ra\'ul Cardoso-Gil, Zihang Liu, Xiao Xu, Rie Y. Umetsu, Ratnamala Chatterjee, Kaustuv Manna

item.title: Grain Boundary Anisotropy and Its Influence on Helium Bubble Nucleation, Growth, and Decohesion in Polycrystalline Iron
item.description: arXiv:2509.07197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The accumulation of helium bubbles at grain boundaries (GBs) critically degrades the mechanical integrity of structural materials in nuclear reactors. While GBs act as sinks for radiation-induced defects, their inherent structural anisotropy leads to complex helium bubble evolution behaviors that remain poorly understood. This work integrates accelerated molecular dynamics simulations and a novel atomic-scale metric, the flexibility volume (V_f), to establish the interplay between GB character, helium segregation, and bubble growth mechanisms in body-centered cubic iron. We demonstrate that V_f, which incorporates both local atomic volume and vibrational properties, qualitatively predicts deformation propensity. Our results reveal that the atomic-scale segregation energy landscape dictates initial helium clustering and subsequent bubble morphology, with low-energy channels in tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary facilitating one-dimensional migration while isolated deep traps in twist {\Sigma}13 boundary promote larger, rounder bubble morphology. Critically, besides gradual bubble growth via trap mutation mechanism, we identify two distinct stress-relief mechanisms: loop punching in anisotropic tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary and interfacial decohesion in twist {\Sigma}11 boundary, with the dominant pathway determined by the interplay between bubble morphology and local mechanical softness. This study establishes a fundamental connection between GB crystallographic and energetical anisotropy and helium bubble evolution, providing critical insights for designing radiation-tolerant microstructures.
item.dc:creator: Yang Zhang, Peter Hatton, Blas P. Uberuaga, Jason R. Trelewicz

item.title: Partially reactive force field for the UiO-66 metal-organic framework
item.description: arXiv:2605.19808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: UiO-66 is the most widely studied metal-organic framework, on account of its structural tunability given by its capacity of sustaining high amounts of point defects in its structure. Its synthesis mechanism is largely unknown, with only a few works mostly focused on the formation of the Zr-oxide cluster. In this work, a partially reactive force field to model UiO-66, nb-UiO-FF, is introduced. This force field incorporates node--ligand reactivity via a Morse potential and the introduction of dummy atoms to reproduce the anisotropic charge distribution of the Zr atoms in the node. nb-UiO-FF reproduces structural features of both UiO-66 and its isoreticular analog UiO-67 as well as framework stability with or without defects, activated or filled with N,N-dimethylformamide or ethanol. Defect generation and node--ligand binding energies are comparable with density functional theory values. The force field is further employed within a molecular dynamics scheme to study the early stages of solvothermal node--ligand binding. Species with structures corresponding to motifs present in UiO-66 are observed, along with other metastable species. This force field enables studying the self-assembly of UiO-66, as well as the formation of its point defects.
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Nawani (Sorbonne Universit\'e, CNRS, Physicochimie des Electrolytes et Nanosyst\`emes Interfaciaux, PHENIX, Paris, France), Rocio Semino (Sorbonne Universit\'e, CNRS, Physicochimie des Electrolytes et Nanosyst\`emes Interfaciaux, PHENIX, Paris, France)

item.title: On representation of macroscopic crack in periodic fine-scale discrete mechanical models
item.description: arXiv:2606.20253v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multiscale modeling of heterogeneous softening materials, boundary conditions (BC) in the fine-scale model strongly influence the strain localization pattern and the macroscopic response. For rectilinear models (e.g., squares or cubes), standard Periodic BCs produce artificially ductile behavior with excessive energy dissipation when the localization band inclination does not match the periodicity directions. Recently proposed Tessellation and Percolation-path-aligned BCs promise to address this by adapting the periodicity frame to align with the evolving localization bands. Alternatively, spherical/circular models provide an orientation independent response by design. Unfortunately, the standard Periodic BCs do not allow development of proper localization band crossing spherical model's boundaries. A recently proposed modification addresses this by adding a displacement jump to the spherical periodic BCs. This study evaluates the applicability of these novel BCs to a mesoscale discrete particle model of concrete. Two-dimensional square and circular models under uniaxial tension with different loading directions are analyzed, with the selected approaches extended to three-dimensional cube models. Results show that Percolation-path-aligned BCs exhibit major shortcomings: they can lead to multiple localization bands due to uneven straining of the two boundary sections and their weakly constrained section can be prone to spurious strain localization. In contrast, Tessellation BCs consistently yield a well-defined localization band, whose length is determined solely by the model geometry, making it straightforward to account for in post-processing. Periodic boundary conditions augmented with a displacement jump applied to a circular model sometimes incorrect produce crack patterns similar to those under the standard Periodic BCs.
item.dc:creator: Jan Raisinger, Jan Eli\'a\v{s}

item.title: Picometre-scale real-time drift correction in TEM and STEM by dynamic control of the specimen stage for atomic-resolution imaging
item.description: arXiv:2608.03344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we show how the specimen drift can be actively compensated by controlling the stage with precision down to the picometre scale. We do this by dynamic control, a generic real-time feedback framework designed to actively stabilize electron microscopy experiments by continuously monitoring an experimental variable from the detector data stream and compensating its evolution during acquisition. The framework, applicable to a broad range of controllable experimental instabilities, includes automated calibration procedures, operates in parallel with image acquisition and is implemented as a software plugin without requiring any hardware modification of the microscope. Results for live drift correction are shown for a selection of TEM and STEM instruments using conventional mechanical stages as well as piezoelectric stages. Experimental results are presented for medium resolution TEM, high-resolution TEM, HR-STEM and in situ observations. With piezoelectric stages, specimen stabilization down to the picometre scale was achieved allowing drift-corrected atomic-resolution imaging. Specimen stage-based stabilization significantly improves long-exposure imaging and in situ experiments by increasing the effective exposure time, preserving the field of view, maintaining identical optical conditions and eliminating the need for numerical alignment of large datasets. Beyond the specific application presented here, dynamic control provides a versatile framework for real-time regulation of electron microscopy experiments and opens new perspectives for quantitative imaging, automated in situ studies and multimodal acquisitions.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Gatel, Julien Dupuy, Teresa Hungria, Martin J. Hytch

item.title: Altermagnetism-Induced Spin-resolved electronic structure in Janus FeX0.5Y0.5 Monolayers (X, Y = S, Se, Te)
item.description: arXiv:2608.09054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Realizing the spin-resolved electronic properties in superconducting materials stands as a critical frontier, offering both novel fundamental physics and potential for dissipationless spin-based devices. Here, we predict a series of Janus FeX0.5Y0.5 monolayers derived from iron-based superconductors (e.g., FeSe, FeTe, and FeS) by using Kondo-type model and first-principles calculations. These Janus structures exhibit significant spin-splittingelectronic states, large topological band gaps (51.4 meV) and high N\'eel temperatures (415 K). We further reveal that valley polarization can be effectively tuned via applied in-plane strain and the resulting valley-polarized anomalous Hall conductivity can be manipulated by shifting the Fermi level. Our work suggests a new strategy based on altermagnetism for engineering spin-splitting states in superconducting systems and inspires further exploration of superconducting spintronics.
item.dc:creator: Mengyang Zhang, Jie Li, Yifei Chen, Shifang Li, Zhentao Fu, Jianxin Zhong

item.title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.09783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $\pi$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ linearly fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP length, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of shorter $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of longer $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific lengths ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the intrinsic structural periodicity and completely delocalized nature of the active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.
item.dc:creator: Tsu-Hsuan Wang, Jeng-Da Chai

item.title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.17987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural network interatomic potential (NNAP) to describe molecular systems using sphmulti, a refined spherical-harmonic basis set that combines extra radial basis with element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel. We further integrate hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria with knowledge-guided key events, enabling the NNAP to retain essential information for describing the material system. For 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan, the resulting NNAP is trained on only 13,680 configurations yet captures key properties, including the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior. NNAP-driven molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that pyrolysis proceeds through furazan-ring opening followed by chain reactions, whereas shock loading induces anisotropic hydrogen transfer driven by interlayer structural deformations. This work enables efficient and reliable MLPs for energetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Guanchen Dong, Huanrong Liu, Lin Wang, Yuxuan Chen, Zhengyu Tu, Qing-an Li, Bin Xu, Jian Li, Shan Zhang, Xiaotong Li, Linghua Tan, Guangcheng Yang, Jun Kang, Rui Su, Pengfei Guan

item.title: Quantum geometry, localization, and topological bounds of spin fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2512.17454v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how topological crystalline defects--dislocations--reshape the real-space quantum geometric tensor and act as tunable sources of quantum geometry. We show that dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and the Hilbert-space geometry of states. We characterize the quantum geometry of topological magnons in ordered arrays of dislocations, demonstrating that defect-induced geometric enhancement controls their localization and topological protection. In disordered arrays, dislocation-driven geometry expands the accessible topological phase space and enables transitions to disorder-induced topological phases. Our results identify the quantum metric as a tunable bridge between crystalline topology, magnonic excitations, and emergent topological matter in aperiodic solid-state and synthetic systems.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Saji, Roberto E. Troncoso

item.title: Anomalous Thermal Conductivity Reversal Driven by a Fluctuating Charge Density Wave
item.description: arXiv:2603.15915v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For more than a century, the lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been known to decrease with increasing temperature, as the phonons that carry heat scatter more strongly via Umklapp processes. Here we report a pronounced violation of this rule in the layered charge-density-wave (CDW) metal 2H-TaSe2. Its in-plane thermal conductivity is strongly nonmonotonic: it peaks sharply at the 122 K ordering transition, collapses to a deep minimum near 210 K, and then anomalously reverses, rising with temperature to at least 350 K. Such a high-temperature reversal, in which a crystal conducts heat more efficiently as it is heated, is rare in crystalline solids. Its thermal conductivity minimum lies deep in the disordered phase well above the ordering transition, unlike the weak, transition-centered anomalies of other charge-density-wave systems, pointing to heat conduction governed by fluctuating rather than established order. Combining inelastic X-ray scattering, selected-area electron diffraction, and synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we attribute the reversal to phonons scattering off persistent, fluctuating charge order that survives more than 150 K above the long-range transition, to at least 300 K. A phenomenological phonon-CDW scattering model, tied directly to the measured diffraction linewidth and intensity, quantitatively reproduces the entire nonmonotonic curve. We also reveal that the charge order melts not abruptly but through a fluctuation- and defect-driven, weak first-order process, leaving short-range correlations far above the transition. This work establishes fluctuating charge order as a sensitive control knob for thermal transport in quantum materials and thermal conductivity as a powerful probe of the hidden charge order.
item.dc:creator: Han Huang, Jinghang Dai, Joyce Christiansen-Salameh, Jiyoung Kim, Samuel Kielar, Desheng Ma, Noah Schinitzer, Danrui Ni, Gustavo Alvarez, Chen Li, Carla Slebodnick, Mario Medina, Bilal Azhar, Ahmet Alatas, Robert Cava, David Muller, Zhiting Tian

item.title: Experimental Observation of Mesoscopic Dynamic Fluctuations in Water-Alcohol Mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2608.30098v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We applied a dynamic fluctuation measurement method to liquid water-methanol mixtures over a wide range of compositions and temperatures. This method, which we developed in recent years, combines ultrasonic and inelastic X-ray scattering techniques to detect mesoscopic-level fluctuations - that is, the degree of heterogeneity - in liquids using sound waves. As a result, it was found that dynamic fluctuations exist across a wide range of compositions and temperatures, including pure substances (water and methanol). Furthermore, in the low-methanol composition range (approximately 20% mol or less), the strength of dynamic fluctuation increased toward lower compositions and lower temperatures, suggesting that the origin of the fluctuation lies in the low temperature (supercooled) region of water alone. Conversely, this indicates that in the range below 20% methanol, fluctuations in water alone are dominant rather than the mixed effects of water and methanol. We performed similar dynamic fluctuation measurements on water-ethanol and water-glycerol mixtures at room temperature. We found that dynamic fluctuations exist universally across the entire composition range, and confirmed an increase in the strength of dynamic fluctuations toward lower compositions in the regions approximately below 15% and below 20%, respectively. This revealed that the phenomenon is not unique to methanol systems but is a common behavior shared by water-alcohol mixtures. It has long been known that water-alcohol mixtures exhibit various thermodynamic anomalies, but the mechanisms behind them have not yet been fully elucidated. The present results are expected to provide a new direction for discussion on this issue.
item.dc:creator: Yukio Kajihara, Nanako Shibata, Masanori Inui

item.title: Superconductivity in a Bulk Moire Superlattice Material
item.description: arXiv:2609.06622v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Moire materials provide a versatile platform realizing emergent electronic states arising from enhanced correlation due to flat bands. A variety of phenomena including superconductivity, low dimensional ferromagnetism, Mott insulating phase, and topological phenomena have been reported in such systems. To date, moire phenomena have been predominantly explored in artificially assembled low dimensional van der Waals structures, where relative twist and lattice alignment are controlled during device fabrication. Recently, intrinsically grown bulk moire crystals have emerged as a complementary materials platform, in which lattice mismatch between constituent layers generates a coherent moire superlattice throughout the bulk crystal. Here, we report the evidence of bulk superconductivity in single crystals of a recently reported bulk Moire material [Sr6TaS8]1+x[TaS2]8 at ambient pressure. The material exhibits a bulk superconducting transition at Tc = 2.5 K, evidenced consistently by electrical transport, magnetic susceptibility, and heat capacity measurements on single crystals. Structural characterization by X-ray diffraction and atomic resolution electron microscopy establishes the composite, incommensurate crystal structure and scanning tunnelling microscopy reveals a long-wavelength surface modulation due to the incommensurate structure. The observation of bulk superconductivity establishes superconductivity as an emergent phase in this intrinsically synthesized moire material and highlights bulk moire crystals as a promising platform for investigating correlated quantum phenomena beyond artificially assembled two-dimensional structures.
item.dc:creator: Subham Naik, Paul Monson, Susanta Manna, Prabuddhakant Mishra, Soumyojit Chatterjee, Sandip Kuila, Partha Pratim Jana, M. B. Sreedhara, Rahul Sharma, Gohil S. Thakur

item.title: Low temperature thermodynamics of $S_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/2$ triangular lattice quantum spin liquid candidate TlYbS$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2609.11881v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometrically frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets exhibit a delicate competition between magnetic order and quantum spin liquid (QSL) behavior, with the Yb-based delafossite family $A$Yb$X_2$ providing a structurally clean platform for exploring this physics. Here, we report a comprehensive study of single-crystal TlYbS$_2$ using DC magnetization, AC susceptibility, electron spin resonance (ESR), and specific heat measurements extending from room temperature to the millikelvin regime. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms a trigonal $R\bar{3}m$ structure comprising well-separated triangular layers of Yb$^{3+}$ ions with no detectable site disorder. At zero field, a weak thermodynamic anomaly is observed near $530$ mK, which may indicate the onset of a weakly ordered state similar to that reported in KYbSe$_2$. Below $300$ mK, the zero-field magnetic specific heat follows $C_{\rm m}\propto T^{1.8}$, close to a quadratic temperature dependence, in contrast to the linear temperature dependence reported for the sister compound TlYbSe$_2$, which has been described in terms of the interplay between spinons and thermally excited gauge-flux excitations. Magnetization and ESR measurements establish pronounced easy-plane magnetic anisotropy, with $g_\perp/g_\parallel \approx 6.9$. The anomaly near $530$ mK exhibits a strongly anisotropic response to magnetic field. For $H\perp c$, it remains visible up to approximately $2$ T and continuously evolves toward a field-induced ordered phase above approximately $2.5$ T, followed by a sequence of field-induced phases that includes a $1/3$ magnetization plateau between approximately $5$ and $8$ T and full polarization near $17$ T. In contrast, for $H\parallel c$, the anomaly weakens and is suppressed near $3$ T, consistent with the recently reported confinement--deconfinement transition from an ordered state to a field-induced QSL.
item.dc:creator: Bishnu P. Belbase, Arjun Unnikrishnan, Piyush Chhallare, Mohan B. Neupane, Eun Sang Choi, Sebastian Erdmann, Muhammad U. Akbar, Mamoun Hemmida, H. -A. Krug von Nidda, Philipp Gegenwart, Arnab Banerjee

item.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
item.description: arXiv:2610.00636v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is constrained by the time and resources required for the underlying experiments or calculations. In computational materials research, repeating the same expensive simulations across agents and trials can make evaluation impractical. We introduce CompMat-Bench, a benchmark of 94 tasks derived from recently published computational materials studies, each asking agents to complete a step toward achieving the study's scientific goal. We reproduce the research steps in advance and assess agents on preparing inputs and analyzing outputs for expensive simulations, so expensive simulations can be avoided during evaluation. The reproduced inputs and results serve as ground truth for grading agents with fixed rules, without an LLM judge. The benchmark supports four evaluation conditions: single tasks and workflows composed of related tasks, each with full or reduced methodological guidance. With full guidance on single tasks, agents based on three LLMs demonstrate the ability to complete individual materials research steps, with pass rates of 66.0-90.4% across 94 tasks. Both longer workflows and reduced guidance can limit agent performance, but in different ways for different agents: they lower the pass rates of the weaker agents, whereas the strongest agent falls only when a long workflow is combined with reduced guidance. Failure analysis attributes most failures to scientific errors rather than to errors in software usage. CompMat-Bench provides a basis for comparing agents on the steps of real materials research and for analyzing agent failure modes.
item.dc:creator: Chenmu Zhang, Levi Felix, Jun-Jie Zhang, Xingfu Li, Xuelian Jiang, Tao Jiang, Subhendu Mishra, Xixi Qin, Boris Yakobson

item.title: Room-Temperature Metallic 2D Ferromagnetism Stabilized by Quantum Metric
item.description: arXiv:2610.19713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The recent discovery of long-sought dice-lattice bands in layered electride YCl opens up unprecedented opportunities for studying correlated electrons in real dice lattice systems. While the weakly dispersive band at the Fermi level is partially filled and density-wave states are expected due to Fermi surface nesting based on conventional theories, the ARPES measurement nevertheless revealed a uniform flat band splitting of 0.5 eV, suggesting unusual ferromagnetism (FM) borne out of the metallic 2D dice lattice. In this Letter, we propose that the uniform metallic FM order is stabilized by the prominent quantum metric near topological band crossing points at K and K', which reconstructs the magnetic instability in the dice metal and tips the density-wave instability toward a uniform FM order. Importantly, our analysis based on random phase approximation (RPA) and Hartree-Fock theory predicts a remarkably high Curie temperature above room temperature for the 2D FM order. These findings establish the first example of a room-temperature 2D metallic magnet stabilized by quantum metric, which not only exemplifies the fundamental significance of quantum geometry in solids but also bears far-reaching applications in energy-efficient high-density magnetic memories.
item.dc:creator: Teng-Fei Ying, Jianqi Zhong, Songyuan Geng, Fangjie Chen, Haoxiang Li, Benjamin T. Zhou
